\chapter{Review --- the Present Tense, Whole}
\label{ch:spanish-review-present-all}
\hlchaptermodality{46}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can conjugate any regular Spanish verb in the present, in any of the three families.}

Eighteen forms, every one built separately before it appeared in the grid.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Review — the present tense, whole}

\label{lesson:ES-C07-repaso-tres-familias}



\begin{quote}
Nothing new in this chapter. Say \textquotedblleft{}we eat\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}we live.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: eighteen forms, and you built each one}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{who} & \textbf{\emph{-ar}} & \textbf{\emph{-er}} & \textbf{\emph{-ir}} \\
\midrule
yo & habl\textbf{o} & com\textbf{o} & viv\textbf{o} \\
tú & habl\textbf{as} & com\textbf{es} & viv\textbf{es} \\
él · ella · usted & habl\textbf{a} & com\textbf{e} & viv\textbf{e} \\
nosotros & habl\textbf{amos} & com\textbf{emos} & viv\textbf{imos} \\
vosotros & habl\textbf{áis} & com\textbf{éis} & viv\textbf{ís} \\
ellos · ustedes & habl\textbf{an} & com\textbf{en} & viv\textbf{en} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{This is the present tense of the Spanish language.} Not a summary of it, not the regular part of it with exceptions pending — every regular verb in Spanish sits in that grid, and there are thousands of them.

Two things are worth reading off it before you close the chapter:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{The \emph{yo} row is the same in all three families.} It always was. That is why the second and third families cost so little when they arrived.
  \item \emph{\textbf{-er\emph{ and }-ir\emph{ differ in exactly two boxes\textbf{ — \emph{nosotros} and \emph{vosotros}. Four of their six forms are identical.}}}}
\end{itemize}

So the whole grid is really one set of endings with a family vowel, plus two exceptions. That is the shape you have actually learned.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item one column straight down — \emph{hablar}, all six
  \item one row straight across — \emph{nosotros}, all three families
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:} Down a column, then across a row, until neither direction stalls.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How many forms are in the grid? (\textbf{Eighteen} — three families, six each.) Which row never varies? (\emph{\textbf{Yo}}.) And how many boxes separate \emph{-er} from \emph{-ir}? (\textbf{Two}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
